bookTitle: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets

facts.statement: A Complex Head and Shoulders reversal pattern features multiple peaks or troughs, such as dual shoulders or a double head, and exhibits a strong structural tendency toward symmetry where a double left shoulder significantly increases the probability of a corresponding double right shoulder.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: A variation of the classic Head and Shoulders reversal pattern where multiple peaks or troughs appear... maintaining a strong tendency toward symmetry.

facts.statement: A Failed Head and Shoulders occurs when a structure develops like a standard reversal pattern, but either prior to or shortly after penetrating the neckline, prices reverse direction, recross the neckline, and resume their original prevailing trend.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: A pattern that initially develops like a standard Head and Shoulders reversal, but... prices reverse direction, recross the neckline, and resume their original trend.

facts.statement: A Head and Shoulders pattern is not complete until prices decisively break the neckline on a closing basis; once broken, a decisive close back across the neckline invalidates the breakdown, confirms a pattern failure, and requires immediate defensive exit of losing positions.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: Once the neckline has been broken, prices must not recross it... traders must exit losing positions immediately to protect capital.

facts.statement: During a Head and Shoulders formation, the head develops on lighter volume than the left shoulder and the right shoulder displays noticeably lighter activity; completion requires expanding volume on the neckline breakout—mandatory for bottoms—followed by light volume on any return pullback.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: The head forms on lighter volume than the left shoulder... On inverse (bottom) Head and Shoulders patterns, a sharp burst of heavy volume on the neckline breakout is mandatory.

facts.statement: In inverse Head and Shoulders bottoms, technical traders frequently initiate early long positions while the right shoulder is still forming, triggered by a 1/2 to 2/3 pullback of the rally from the head, a drop to the left shoulder price level, or a short-term down trendline break.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: Common entry triggers include a 1/2 to 2/3 pullback of the rally from the head, a decline to the price level of the left shoulder, or the breaking of a short-term down trendline.

facts.statement: The minimum price objective for a Head and Shoulders pattern is calculated by measuring the vertical height between the head apex and the directly vertical point on the neckline, then projecting that distance from the closing neckline breakout price, while the maximum objective is a 100% retracement of the prior trend.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: The price target is derived from the vertical height of the pattern projected from the breakout point... This target represents a minimum price objective.

variables.definition: Exact price point where the neckline is penetrated on a closing basis
Extreme price reached at the apex of the head
Price level along the neckline directly vertical to the head apex

facts.statement: An alternative measuring technique projects the minimum price objective of a Head and Shoulders reversal by doubling the vertical distance between the extreme price of the head and the subsequent reaction trough D, then adding or subtracting that value from the breakout price.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: Alternative Wave Projection Formula: Price Objective = Breakout Price +/- (2 x |Price_Head - Price_Trough D|).

variables.definition: Exact price point where the neckline is penetrated on a closing basis
Extreme price reached at the apex of the head
Price level at the reaction trough immediately following the head

facts.statement: General Motors demonstrated a daily continuation inverse Head and Shoulders within an existing uptrend that completed upon a decisive close above the 60 neckline, whereas Dow Jones & Co. formed a 10-year monthly Head and Shoulders bottom (1988–1997) whose right shoulder formed an ascending triangle before breaking out above 42.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: General Motors (Daily Chart): completed upon a close above the 60 neckline... Dow Jones & Co. (Monthly Chart): 10-year major Head and Shoulders bottom (1988–1997)... breaking out above 42.

facts.topic: Nike and Forest Labs Textbook Patterns
facts.statement: Weekly chart case studies of Nike Inc. and Forest Labs Inc. illustrate classic reversal mechanics: Nike formed a top with equal shoulders, a higher head, declining peak volume, and a scheduled neckline return move, while Forest Labs formed an inverse bottom with a slightly down-slanting neckline and post-breakout pullback.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: Nike Inc. (Weekly Chart): Illustrated a textbook Head and Shoulders top... Forest Labs Inc. (Weekly Chart): Showed an inverse Head and Shoulders bottom with a slightly down-slanting neckline.

facts.statement: A 1995 Federal Reserve Bank of New York staff report titled 'Head and Shoulders: Not Just a Flaky Pattern' provided formal mathematical and empirical verification confirming the predictive validity of the Head and Shoulders chart formation in foreign exchange markets.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: Federal Reserve Bank of New York study titled 'Head and Shoulders: Not Just a Flaky Pattern,' which mathematically confirmed the predictive validity of the pattern in foreign exchange markets.

facts.statement: A Triple Top or Triple Bottom is a major trend reversal pattern featuring three prominent peaks or troughs at approximately the same price level, functioning as a minor structural variation of the Head and Shoulders pattern where the middle extreme matches the outer two in height and carries identical forecasting implications.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: A major trend reversal pattern consisting of three prominent peaks or troughs occurring at approximately the same price level... minor structural variation of the Head and Shoulders pattern.

facts.statement: A Triple Top is formally completed only when support levels across both intervening reaction lows are broken on a closing basis, whereas a Triple Bottom requires a closing penetration through both intervening rally peaks, though breaking the nearest intervening peak or trough can serve as an early reversal signal.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: Complete only when support levels along both intervening reaction lows have been broken on a closing basis... Triple Bottom Confirmation: Complete only when prices close through both intervening rally peaks.

facts.statement: In Triple Tops and Bottoms, trading volume diminishes across each successive peak or trough during pattern development, followed by heavy downside volume at a top breakdown or a mandatory sharp burst of upside volume at a bottom breakout, with common return pullbacks to broken support or resistance offering secondary entries.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: Volume tends to diminish with each successive peak or trough... A return move back to the broken support or resistance line following the breakout is common and provides a secondary entry opportunity.

facts.topic: Triple Top and Bottom Price Target
facts.statement: The price target for a Triple Top or Triple Bottom is determined by calculating the vertical height between the horizontal price level of the three peaks and the lowest intervening reaction trough, then adding that height to the breakout price for bottoms or subtracting it from the breakdown price for tops.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Reversal Patterns: Triple/Double Tops & Bottoms, Saucers & Spikes
sourceCitation.excerpt: Pattern Height (H) = Price_Peaks - Price_Lowest Trough; Downside Target = Breakdown Price - H; Upside Target = Breakout Price + H.

generalAssumptions: Market action discounts all known and unknown fundamentals.
Prices move in trends, and a trend in motion is more likely to continue than to reverse.
Chart reversal patterns exhibit structural symmetry and require volume confirmation and closing price penetration to validate trend changes.
